messages:
rafa: FYI we started seeing very different prefix cache behavior between Hosted and Private after yesterday's runtime change. Hosted steady ~78% for short prefixes; a Private cluster sampled at ~46% and token p95 doubled on a few routes.

tanvi: hmm. what changed in the rollout? any keying tweaks?

rafa: rollout included: kernel-selector tweaks, new batching heuristic, and a change to KV key normalization (trim trailing spaces + collapse repeated inner spaces). That helped Hosted but Private shows increased key diversity. Logs below.

sam: can you paste the probe numbers so we can see if it's lookup cost vs key mismatch?

rafa: probe snippet (both envs, truncated):

```
Hosted:
  total_prefixes: 118400
  unique_cache_keys: 27000
  hit_rate: 0.78
  avg_lookup_ms: 0.95
  p95_lookup_ms: 2.3

Private (vpc-netstore):
  total_prefixes: 102100
  unique_cache_keys: 62100
  hit_rate: 0.46
  avg_lookup_ms: 5.2
  p95_lookup_ms: 13.1
```

rafa: private avg_lookup_ms includes netstore fetchs (our NFS gateway). Also seeing many more key variants per prefix.

tanvi: that smells like normalization mismatch or caller-side whitespace/zero-width chars. Did the SDK change ship to callers too? Tokenization differences could amplify variants.

infra-bot: deploy 1953.1 applied to runtime-prod-hosted at 2026-03-16T02:14:00Z

sam: I profiled the private run: most extra time in netstore roundtrips + repeated TLS handshakes under high concurrency. The batching heuristic increased parallel lookups which amplifies network tails.

jess: so two separate problems: (1) normalization/keying causing unique keys -> lower hits; (2) netstore RPCs + more parallelism -> larger tail. Different mitigations.

rafa: proposed immediate mitigations:
  - rollback key-normalization only on Private pipeline via feature-flag.
  - deploy a lightweight client-side canonicalizer for messy prompts (strip zero-width, normalize unicode quotes) as an interim.
  - add netstore-aware lookup throttling when store is non-local (config per deployment class).
  - enable passive sampling (0.5% of requests) to export pre-normalization prefix -> computed key mapping for analysis.

tanvi: +1. Also let's compute per-prefix entropy and export top-100 high-entropy prefixes to find noisy callers.

sam: for throttling I'll add a circuit to switch to serialized lookups when netstore RTT p95 > 8ms. That should avoid TLS churn and reduce connection storms.

ops-bot: incident INC-2026-042 created: private prefix-cache hit regression. Assigned: @rafa @sam @tanvi

rafa: quick canary after flipping the flag on private-canary-03: hit_rate jumped 46% -> 74% within 10 minutes, token p95 down ~40%. So normalization change was primary.

jess: good signal. Still want throttling; keep batching heuristic, but with netstore-aware knobs.

tanvi: curious why Hosted didn't regress with the normalization change earlier. Hypothesis: hosted path uses S3 gateway with connection pooling and a request de-dup layer which collapsed simultaneous fetches and amortized TLS. Private NFS gateway doesn't dedupe parallel fetches and opens new connections.

sam: noted. I'll open PRs: (a) feature-flag rollback for Private, (b) netstore-aware lookup throttling, (c) probe sampler + entropy exporter. Add perf CI that simulates high netstore RTTs.

rafa: thanks. next steps: sam opens PR, tanvi wires dashboards and export, jess coordinates rollback window with infra. I'll draft a short postmortem once fixes land.

sam: PR 4829 opened: runtime: netstore-aware lookup throttling + feature-flagged normalization. https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4829

rafa: running canary now. early numbers look promising.

jess: :thumbsup: keep updates in this thread. If canary stable for 30m, proceed with gradual rollout plan.

rafa: will update. thanks team.
